title: Resourcefulness and blaming the outside
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Are you working from your most resourceful state today?
I said that one thing I always ask myself is: am I working from a state of maximum resourcefulness? Am I working in a place that I love?
I said that we memorize people: we do not say you are different today, we say it is the same old person, and that I try to see what is new.
A student asked Jose: when you look back at your failures, was it an external thing or something about your internal actions?

I said that the minute people start blaming things externally, that is negative language and a very dangerous situation, because they are not fully taking accountability, and the language comes from a negative anchor.
A student said: you can choose to lose or choose to win, but even in trying to win you have to be willing to lose.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how resourceful you feel today from one to ten.
Write the people you have fixed in your mind.
Write what you blame outside yourself.
Write what you would own instead.

check.q: What did I say I ask myself?
choices: Am I in a state of maximum resourcefulness

check.q: What did I say blaming externally shows?
What did a student say about winning?
choices: You must be willing to lose

recap: Work from your most resourceful state. Own what is yours.
